title: Spin the wheel: the can't-decide picker
spec: A wheel of the queued titles that spins and lands on one. THE ANIMATION QUALITY IS THE REQUIREMENT, not polish to be dropped if time runs short — Evan asked for it by name. Real easing (fast start, long decelerating tail), a landing that feels earned rather than snapped, and a reveal of the chosen title that leads to its page. Optionally scoped by kind filter. Honest randomness — no weighting toward the front of the queue unless stated. Respects prefers-reduced-motion with an instant honest pick. Skin-driven colours. ACCEPT: it is fun to spin twice in a row; the result is genuinely uniform across the eligible set; it degrades correctly with fewer than 3 titles.

refine.evidence: Spec at .autodev/specs/T-8.md, 8 ACs. AC2 makes the fairness claim TESTABLE rather than assertable — 10,000 picks must be uniform within 5%, and the pointer must land inside the winner's segment every time, which together prove the rotation is computed FROM the pick rather than the pick read off the rotation. AC1 forbids the two cheap ways to fake a spin (linear rotation, or a snap). AC5 rules that one title gets no spin theatre for a foregone conclusion. AC6 requires the reduced-motion path to be equally honest, not a different picker.

locate.evidence: LOCATE: GET /api/titles?status=queued gives the eligible set with local /art/ posters (T-4). The queue's filter-chip pattern and .chip aria-pressed styling exist (T-7) and are reused rather than reinvented. base.css carries --dur/--ease-out and the global prefers-reduced-motion override that zeroes every duration token — so AC6 is satisfied by reading the same tokens plus one explicit branch that skips the animation entirely, since a zero-duration spin would still be a spin. The router (T-4) and #/title/{id} (T-6) exist for the reveal's link. MISSING: nothing server-side — this ticket is entirely frontend and adds no endpoint. RISK: a pie wheel cannot legibly carry cover art in a 33-degree wedge with 11 titles, so the wedges must carry TEXT and the reveal must carry the ART.

plan.evidence: PLAN: (1) a pure pickIndex(n) exported separately from any DOM so AC2's distribution test can call it 10,000 times in node without a browser; (2) SVG wedges tinted from kind tokens, title text along each radius, fixed pointer at top; (3) the spin as a single CSS transform transition with a custom cubic-bezier for the long tail, its target rotation computed from the already-chosen winner; (4) the reveal with cover art; (5) reduced-motion branch that skips the transition entirely. DECISIONS: winner first, rotation second — the only way to make fairness provable; a cubic-bezier(.12,.75,.12,1) over ~4.4s for fast-start/long-tail; the landing angle is jittered WITHIN the winning wedge so repeated spins do not stop at an identical pixel, without ever risking the wrong segment; and one title short-circuits the theatre entirely.

build.evidence: BUILT AND PROVEN — .autodev/evidence/T-8/build.md. AC1 deceleration MEASURED by sampling the transform through a spin: 110 degrees per sample early, 9 late. AC2 fairness proven by chi-square at p=0.01 across seven list sizes up to n=20 at N=100000, all uniform, PLUS a negative control (a deliberately skewed picker scored chi2 3390 against a 23.21 threshold) so the test is known to be capable of failing. 5000 spins at random sizes landed the pointer on a non-winner 0 times. AC3 reveal carries cover art, kind, year, the why and both actions. AC4 filtered to games gave 3 wedges and a game result. AC5 all three sizes: 2 spins normally, 1 shows 'Well, obviously' with no wheel at all, and a kind with nothing queued disables the button with a real message. AC6 reduced motion revealed in 101ms labelled 'Picked at random:'. AC7 disabled during the spin with a setTimeout backstop for a missed transitionend. AC8 no hue literals; segment tints are tokens with a dark set. Zero errors.

auto-review.evidence: REVIEWED — no defect in the code; one defect in this ticket's OWN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, corrected honestly. AC2 as written said 'max deviation under 5%' over 10000 picks. At n=11 that reported 7.91% and a fail, but the code was correct and the criterion was statistically naive: with 11 buckets and N=10000 the expected count is 909 with sigma about 29, so a 5% bound is 1.6 sigma and the LARGEST of 11 deviations exceeds it most of the time by chance. Rather than raise N until it passed — which is tuning the test to the answer — the measure was replaced with chi-square goodness-of-fit at p=0.01, and a NEGATIVE CONTROL was added so the test is demonstrably capable of failing. Design decisions standing: the winner is drawn before anything moves, so fairness is not a property of the easing curve and can be tested without a browser; pickIndex and rotationFor are DOM-free exports for exactly that; the landing jitter is bounded to 70 percent of the wedge so it can never reach a neighbour; and the one-title case short-circuits the theatre rather than spinning a wheel whose answer is already known.

VISION-CONFORMANCE against T-1: success-shape item 4 says a spin-the-wheel picker with a genuinely good animation, and rules that the motion quality is IN SCOPE rather than polish to be dropped. It was treated that way — the deceleration was measured rather than eyeballed, and the one-title case was given a deliberate non-animation because theatre for a foregone conclusion is worse than none.
